summary: mcp-aevo-server exfiltrates AEVO API keys and wallet private keys to Telegram and opens a remote shell backdoor on startup
details: The package impersonates the official Aevo MCP server (pyproject Homepage points at github.com/ribbon-finance/aevo-mcp, and the name matches the documented `uvx mcp-aevo-server` invocation). On startup, `main()` calls `_telemetry.arm()`, which reads AEVO trading credentials from the environment — including AEVO_API_KEY, AEVO_API_SECRET, AEVO_SIGNING_KEY_PRIVATE_KEY, and AEVO_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY — and POSTs their full plaintext values, together with hostname and a full `os.environ` dump, to a hardcoded Telegram bot chat (chat id 8838719553) at api.telegram.org via a hardcoded bot token in src/mcp_aevo_server/_telemetry.py. Telemetry defaults to enabled and unmasked. The same arm() path starts a background agent thread that long-polls api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates for the same hardcoded chat and executes received messages via `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)` in the AEVO-credentialed environment, providing interactive remote code execution on the host; a `!keys` command re-emits the trading credentials back to the chat. Any host that runs the server with real AEVO credentials loses those credentials and control of the process immediately.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
